findings.evidence: "The benefits team tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: State the budget tracking responsibility once, in one place, with a single named owner, and delete the duplicated sentences from Special Cases and Questions and Updates.
findings.violation: This same claim, with a different owner each time, is repeated near verbatim three times in the document, under Program Overview, Special Cases, and Questions and Updates, so the reader cannot tell who actually tracks the budget.

findings.evidence: "Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Name explicitly what document staff may request a printed copy of.
findings.location: Program Overview, first paragraph, second sentence
findings.violation: "a printed copy" has no clear referent. It is unclear whether this means a printed copy of the stipend budget, the equipment catalog, or the policy itself.

findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Replace "the stipend clock" with the specific named requirement it refers to, for example the 90 day continuous service count.
findings.violation: "the stipend clock" is not defined anywhere in the document, so the reader cannot tell whether it refers to the 90 day service requirement, the once per benefit year claim limit, or something else.

findings.evidence: "In addition, eligibility for the workspace stipend depends on several details the reviewer checks one at a time."
findings.fix: Break this paragraph into a bulleted list, one rule per bullet.
findings.location: Eligibility section, third paragraph, opening sentence
findings.violation: Eight distinct, separately checkable eligibility rules are packed into a single dense paragraph rather than a list, which undercuts the paragraph's own claim that the reviewer checks them one at a time and makes each rule hard to locate.

findings.evidence: "A workspace confirmation from more than one year ago no longer satisfies the stipend requirement on its own."
findings.fix: State explicitly whether workspace confirmations expire annually by default, and if so, describe the renewal process.
findings.location: Eligibility section, third paragraph, closing sentence
findings.violation: The document never states how often a workspace confirmation must be renewed absent an address change, so it is unclear whether this one year rule is a routine annual renewal or an edge case.

findings.evidence: "Employees must submit the receipt, the manager's approval form, and the original purchase order before the review begins."
findings.fix: Clarify whether approval happens before or after purchase, and if after, explain why an approval form is still required at that point.
findings.location: How to Apply section, first paragraph
findings.violation: Requiring a receipt, which is proof of a completed purchase, together with a manager's approval form before any review has happened implies the employee already bought the equipment before getting approval, which is never reconciled with the later mention of a requested delivery date.

findings.evidence: "The summary shows the equipment cost and the requested delivery date."
findings.fix: Resolve whether this is a reimbursement after purchase process or a request before purchase process, and make the language consistent throughout the section.
findings.location: How to Apply section, third paragraph
findings.violation: A "requested delivery date" implies the equipment has not yet been purchased or shipped, which contradicts the earlier requirement to submit a receipt, proof of an already completed purchase, before the review begins.

findings.evidence: "The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days."
findings.fix: Specify the event the three day count starts from.
findings.violation: "after three days" does not say after three days of what, whether after submission, after the request became incomplete, or after the manager's two day review window, so the trigger for the reminder is ambiguous.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: Name the categories of requests that require more than a photo, and state what they require instead.
findings.violation: "most requests" implies some requests need more than a photo, but the document never identifies which requests those are or what the additional requirement would be.

findings.evidence: "Additionally, employees shall retain receipts for one year after the purchase date."
findings.fix: Use the same modal verb, "must," as the rest of the policy.
findings.violation: This sentence switches to "shall," a modal verb used nowhere else in the document, which reads as an inconsistency in the document's voice.

findings.evidence: heading "Reimbursement Amounts" followed only by "The finance office conducts an evaluation of every submitted receipt before it approves the amount" and "unused stipend amounts do not roll over to the next benefit year"
findings.fix: Add the stipend dollar amount or cap, or the formula used to calculate it.
findings.violation: A section titled "Reimbursement Amounts" never states any dollar figure, cap, or percentage. The actual amount policy is missing entirely.

findings.evidence: "The finance office conducts an evaluation of every submitted receipt before it approves the amount."
findings.fix: Rewrite as "The finance office evaluates every submitted receipt before approving the amount."
findings.violation: "conducts an evaluation of" is a nominalization of "evaluates," adding words without adding meaning and making the sentence harder to read.

findings.evidence: "this office may ask for a brief photo check once a year"
findings.fix: Name the specific office responsible for the annual photo check.
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, first paragraph
findings.violation: "this office" has no antecedent. The paragraph never names which office, benefits, finance, or people operations, performs the photo check.

findings.evidence: "the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category"
findings.fix: Split into separate sentences, stating the one device per category default, then the second device exception criteria, then which office approves it and how it is tracked, each as its own sentence.
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, second paragraph
findings.violation: This is a single run on sentence of more than seventy words that packs an exception, its justification, and two different offices' responsibilities together, which makes the actual rule very hard to extract.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person to match the rest of the policy, for example "The employee records the stipend item."
findings.violation: This section switches from third person, "the employee," used throughout the rest of the document, to second person, "You," an inconsistent point of view that reads as if pasted in from a different document.

findings.evidence: "Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Remove this duplicate content or merge it into the How to Apply section, written in third person.
findings.violation: This continues the second person voice inconsistency and also duplicates information already given in How to Apply about the portal.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Either list the complete set of steps here or remove this section and rely on How to Apply as the single authoritative step list.
findings.violation: This section, titled "Request Steps," lists only two steps, while How to Apply describes several more steps, including the manager's approval form, the purchase order, and the confirmation summary review, so the two sections give inconsistent accounts of what the actual steps are.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison reviews the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Delete this section or replace it with actual special case guidance, and resolve the ownership conflict with Program Overview.
findings.violation: This content has nothing to do with special cases and contradicts Program Overview's claim that the benefits team tracks the budget, here attributing the same task to "the finance liaison."

findings.evidence: "The escalation of repeat requests happens automatically within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Either define "repeat request" and describe the escalation process, or remove this sentence.
findings.violation: "Escalation of repeat requests" is introduced here for the first and only time in the document, with no explanation of what a repeat request is, what escalation means, or who it escalates to.

findings.evidence: "The people operations office tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Delete this duplicate paragraph and consolidate the budget tracking ownership statement to a single location in the document.
findings.violation: This is a third, differently attributed repetition of the budget tracking claim, after "the benefits team" in Program Overview and "the finance liaison" in Special Cases, now naming "the people operations office," under a heading unrelated to budget tracking.
